subject.title: feat: add jsonl support to memory indexer

question: Should builtin memorySearch.extraPaths ingest arbitrary JSONL raw message logs, or should JSONL recall stay in QMD/session-memory, a converter, or plugin/API-owned workflow?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but widening builtin ingestion changes sensitive memory visibility and conflicts with lean-core/plugin-boundary guidance unless maintainers explicitly sponsor the core behavior.

options.title: Document Supported Alternative
options.body: Keep builtin extraPaths Markdown/multimodal-only and document QMD session indexing, converter, or plugin workflows for raw JSONL recall.

options.title: Add Native Builtin JSONL
options.body: Implement JSONL as a first-class builtin memory format with line-aware chunks, memory_get support, watcher coverage, tests, docs, and privacy guardrails.

options.title: Design Plugin/API First
options.body: Leave this issue open until maintainers decide whether a plugin or memory API extension should own arbitrary raw-log ingestion.

recommendation.title: Document Supported Alternative
recommendation.body: Keep builtin extraPaths Markdown/multimodal-only and document QMD session indexing, converter, or plugin workflows for raw JSONL recall.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already supplied the active keep-open analysis and has the strongest recent history around the affected memory host/runtime boundary.
